about.title: Monterey Park Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey Park sees hundreds of injury collisions each year, with public crash records pointing to Garfield Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, Garvey Avenue, and the SR-60 corridor as frequent sites of reported crashes, many clustering on Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the period right after matters: insurers move quickly, memories fade, and physical evidence like skid marks or damaged vehicle parts can disappear. We're a personal injury team that evaluates what happened, deals with insurance adjusters, and explains your options under California law. There's no cost to you unless your case results in a recovery. Reaching out early gives your case the best chance of being built on solid ground before details are lost.

whyChoose.title: Why Monterey Park Residents Reach Out Early

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Closer Than It Feels
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to gather facts can quietly cost you your right to file.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Isn't the End
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a crash on Atlantic Boulevard or Garvey Avenue, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: California places no cap on compensation for pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless you recover money.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements later to minimize what they owe you. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: Are certain roads in Monterey Park more likely to have reported crashes?
items.answer: Public crash records show that Garfield Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, Garvey Avenue, and the SR-60 freeway corridor have higher collision counts than other streets in the city. This is a neutral observation based on reported data, not a judgment about any road's safety.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney about my case?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free case review, and we work on contingency — meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost to you at any point.
